title: Deformation and integration factors under a coordinate chart
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $n\geq1$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $Y$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme, let $h:U\to Y$ be smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $e:U\to A=\mathbf A^d_Y$ be an etale $Y$-map, where $U$ is finite type over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Put $p:A\to Y$, so $h=pe$. Use fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] $W=U\times_YU$, $W_A=A\times_YA$, with first projections $p_U,p_A$ and diagonal closed immersions $\Delta_U,\Delta_A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $Z=U\times_AU\subset W$ and $O=W\setminus(Z\setminus\Delta_U(U))$, with its induced open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Write $i:O\hookrightarrow W$ and $q=(e\times e)|_O:O\to W_A$. Use the constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], derived pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $\omega_g=Rg^!\Lambda_{\operatorname{target}(g)}$. For any smooth separated finite-type $g$ with closed section $s$, put $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ [def-pur-section-invariant]. Let $N_U=N_{\Delta_U/W}$ and $N_A=N_{\Delta_A/W_A}$, with projections $\pi_U,\pi_A$ and zero sections $z_U,z_A$ [def-pur-normal-bundle, lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. Use the actual normal-bundle isomorphism $N_U\xrightarrow{\sim}U\times_A N_A$ induced by the graded conormal pullback [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change], which identifies with $de$ on the tangent bundles. Let $a:C(p_U,\Delta_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*C(p_A,\Delta_A)$ be open restriction to $O$ followed by the canonical etale exceptional comparison for $q$, and let $b:C(\pi_U,z_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*C(\pi_A,z_A)$ be the corresponding comparison for this actual pullback bundle. These use the canonical etale exceptional identification and exceptional composition [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality].

Write $\delta_h,\delta_p$ for the uniquely normalized DNC maps of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] for these diagonal sections, and write $\beta_h,\beta_p$ for the zero-section restrictions of the inverse integration-transposed vector-bundle purity maps [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity, lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], with targets $\Lambda_U(d)[2d]$ and $\Lambda_A(d)[2d]$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Then, with canonical Tate pullback [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists],
$$b\circ\delta_h=(Le^*\delta_p)\circ a,\qquad \beta_h=(Le^*\beta_p)\circ b.$$
The DNC comparisons in the first identity are normalized to the identity on the standard section invariant, with deformation coordinates $u_i=x_i/t$ [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry], and its normal comparison is the actual differential specified above. The second identity concerns the actual ordinary-etale integration trace transported to the specified pro-etale category, and remains valid under any further invertible linear change of normal frame [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]. Thus neither identity has a scalar or sign ambiguity. They hold in the derived category, including the identity normalization at $d=0$.

proof.text: Use the already proved geometric constructions, now reexported from ChartDncVectorFactorData. Apply lem-pur-chart-dnc-naturality to get the exact first factor equation without an integration hypothesis.

Apply lem-pur-chart-integration-adjoints to the forward zero-section transpose equation. Postcompose with inverse Tate and precompose with beta_U inverse; cancellation and preservation of inverses by derived pullback give beta_U = normal followed by e*beta_A followed by Tate. No DNC map occurs in this calculation.

For every open W, frame f and automorphism G, apply bundleOrientation_frames to G followed by f. In beta inverse followed by normalBundleComparison cancel the latter isomorphism. The remaining map is nu* of bundleSectionAdjoint. Naturality of the explicit pullComparison natural isomorphism moves this adjoint through W restriction; functoriality transports the frame equation and proves FrameIndependence. All ranks and empty schemes are retained.
